messages:
carol (AE): Polaris Finance asked for a concise multi-SLA perf proof. Requirements: sustained 140 qps chat (seq ~512), brief multi-az spikes up to 1000 qps, and a clear SLO table for p95/p99/p99.9 comparing redwood-7b-fp32, redwood-7b-4bit, and a new redwood-7b-int8 variant they want to evaluate. They also want reproducible CI steps, a short security note about prompt retention, and multi-region failover notes. Can we scope a run and give a ballpark cost + recommended deployment?

hamid (SRE): Proposed plan: warm 20m to populate KV cache, steady-state 45m @140 qps, then burst steps: 2m@300, 3m@500, 5m@800, 5m@1000, then cooldown 12m. We'll run across two regions (us-east & eu-west) in parallel to validate cross-region routing and failover. Metrics: p50/p95/p99/p99.9 per-route, gpu slice util, batch size distribution, kv_cache_hit, inter-region failover latency. Tag runs customer=polaris bench=multi-az-quant.

rachel (SE): Important: Polaris requires <200ms p95 for chat during steady and wants p95 <350ms during burst if possible. Note that int8 may have different kernel perf and memory pressure; batching behavior can change tail. We'll include explicit warm vs cold cache runs for each quantization variant and run the int8 variant with conservative batch targets.

tyler (Solutions Eng): Quick token math: assume avg output 70 tok/resp. Steady 140 qps -> 9.8k tok/s => ~846M tok/day if sustained. Embeddings load? Polaris said background embedding indexing at 30 qps with 1024 tokens per embedding request. That flips totals: embed 30*1024=30.7k tok/s additional; embeddings dominate volume. We'll flag that in cost appendix. Pricing rough: use list-rate illustrative numbers: fp32 $0.0000010/token, 4bit $0.00000036/token, int8 $0.00000028/token (est). I'll prepare a short spreadsheet.

hamid (SRE): Bench profile summary:
```
- variants: [redwood-7b-fp32, redwood-7b-4bit, redwood-7b-int8]
- chat_seq: 512 (prompt 128 / resp 384 avg)
- embed_seq: 1024 for embedding route
- qps_profile: chat steady 140, chat bursts [300,500,800,1000], embed steady 30 qps
- batch_targets: {fp32:16, 4bit:8, int8:10, embed:32}
- warmup: populate chat kv cache with 10k sample prompts per region
- metrics: latency_histogram_ms, gpu_util_pct, batch_size_hist, kv_hit_ratio, inter_region_failover_ms
```

carol (AE): Polaris auditors will want the exact CI command that created artifacts. Please paste the command we should provide. Also they want a redact proof showing we didn't store raw prompts.

hamid (SRE): Pasteable CI command (single-line example to drop in their CI):
```bash
./ci/bench_runner \
  --profile profiles/polaris_multi_az_quant.json \
  --models redwood-7b-fp32,redwood-7b-4bit,redwood-7b-int8 \
  --duration 5400 \
  --output gs://redwood-temp/polaris/results/ \
  --meta "customer=polaris,run=multi-az-quant" \
  --regions us-east-1,eu-west-1 \
  --redact-prompts true
```
Redact flag stores only input hashes + token counts; full redact-manifest and deletion logs will be produced. We'll also produce an HSM/KMS note.

rachel (SE): Note on multi-az: we'll simulate failover during steady-state by cutting region routing for 90s and measuring inter-region reroute latency and tail impacts. That will show how quickly client traffic shifts and whether cold-start on the other region spikes tail.

tyler (Solutions Eng): Ops note: suggest enabling routing fallback policy that can route new burst traffic to int8 or 4bit if fp32 slices saturated. We'll capture the effect of fallback on p99.9 in the results.

audit-bot: audit: redact manifest will be written to gs://redwood-temp/polaris/audit/redact-manifest-4490001234.json; access log window: 7 days; retention of artifacts: 30 days.

hamid (SRE): interim: steady 45m @140 qps in us-east on 4bit complete. Steady numbers (4bit, warm): p95 135ms, p99 340ms, p99.9 670ms. embed steady p95 42ms. gpu_util ~64%, batch median 8, kv_hit ~71%. No dropped reqs. Uploading partials to gs://redwood-temp/polaris/partial/4bit-us-east.json

rachel (SE): Good. Can you run int8 next and then fp32? We'll compare warm cache behavior.

hamid (SRE): queued int8 then fp32 across both regions. Scheduling failover test after model runs.

hamid (SRE): final: runs complete and multi-az failover executed. Topline aggregated numbers: 
- redwood-7b-4bit (warm): steady p95 140ms, burst@1000 p95 560ms, burst@1000 p99.9 1.3s
- redwood-7b-int8 (warm): steady p95 125ms, burst@1000 p95 480ms, burst@1000 p99.9 1.1s (int8 slightly better tail than 4bit in our config)
- redwood-7b-fp32 (warm): steady p95 98ms, burst@1000 p95 260ms, burst@1000 p99.9 720ms
Inter-region failover: when we blackholed us-east for 90s, traffic rerouted to eu-west within 12s median; temporary p99.9 spike observed ~1.8s while caches warmed.

tyler (Solutions Eng): Cost delta observed in these runs: fp32 ~3.4x per-token cost vs 4bit; int8 ~0.78x of 4bit per-token cost (so int8 appears more cost-effective per-token in our test). But note int8 may require more careful tuning in production. We'll provide appendix with per-hour slice estimates and token totals including embedding volume.

rachel (SE): Recommendation: For Polaris Finance (high embedding volume + chat), a hybrid approach looks best: keep embeddings on 1b-4bit (cheap), use fp32 for primary chat traffic only when strict tail required (dedicated slices in primary region), and use int8 as a mid-tier for cost-sensitive bursts after verification. For multi-az resilience enable pre-warm in secondary region just before predicted maintenance windows to avoid the 1.8s tail spike.

carol (AE): Can someone own the writeup + deck for Monday customer meeting? Need 1-pager, heatmaps, failover graph, and cost appendix. Also include redact proof and HSM note.

rachel (SE): I'll own the writeup and deck. Template: TL;DR, test config, p95/p99/p99.9 tables, heatmaps (qps vs latency), failover timeline graph, cost appendix, recommendation. ETA Monday 10:00 PT.

tyler (Solutions Eng): I'll finalize the cost spreadsheet and include hosted vs dedicated commit scenarios. Also include an ops note about KMS/HSM overhead if they request FIPS/HSM proofs.

audit-bot: artifacts uploaded and permissions set: gs://redwood-temp/polaris/final/; redact manifest and deletion logs included.

hamid (SRE): All artifacts are uploaded and CI profile is in gs://redwood-temp/polaris/profiles/. Closing thread once deck posted.

carol (AE): Thanks team. Action items: hamid add final links to deck, rachel draft & post writeup, tyler finalize cost appendix, carol prep customer sync. :rocket:
